text:
maya: FYI - after yesterday's deploy we're seeing several nodes in eu-west1 with a single GPU-heavy pod each, blocking newer batch runs. Jobs stuck Pending. Anyone else?
jon: yep. looks like a mix of required podAntiAffinity + nodeSelector:gpu-arch=ampere. leaves tiny one-pod islands.
leo: and many of the pods tolerate the taint gpu.workload=dedicated:NoSchedule so they won't be evicted by default.
anuj: do we have events for one of the Pending jobs? paste please.
maya: pulled one: 
maya: kubectl describe pod batch-x-77 -n ml | sed -n '1,120p'
maya: Events:
  Type    Reason       Age   From               Message
  ----    ------       ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled    12m   default-scheduler  Successfully assigned ml/batch-x-77 to node-gpu-eu-west1-b-09
  Warning FailedMount  11m   kubelet            MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "scratch-local" : node affinity mismatch
jon: ah, local PV is preventing relocation. that plus the NoSchedule taint makes nodes sticky.
sam: cost angle: some AZs are at 95% while others have spare reserved GPUs. imbalance is causing us to spin extra on-demand in other regions. billing shows a 7% uptick.
descheduler-bot: suggested action: run RemoveDuplicates + LowNodeUtilization strategies. exclude pods with annotation "scratch-local=true" and ignore system namespaces.
leo: quick count: grep of tolerations shows ~14 pods across 5 nodes with that taint and local PV.
anuj: root cause summary: (1) strict podAntiAffinity for training jobs, (2) dedicated taint tolerated by training pods, (3) local PVs preventing eviction, (4) kube-scheduler not preempting because preempting would violate PV/node affinity.
maya: short-term ops question: relax anti-affinity for batch queue?
jon: proposal: canary descheduler tonight to evict duplicates and low-util batch pods that do not reference local PVs. also add node labels to mark batch-consolidatable nodes.
sam: agree but add guardrails: alert if PodPreemptionRate > 3/min or PendingBatchJobs > 150 for >10m. rollback if triggers.
leo: perf caveat: packing two heavy GPU jobs onto same NVLink domain increased p95 latency in a prior test. we should run a microbench after canary.
anuj: long-term: (A) admission webhook to convert requiredDuringScheduling anti-affinity to preferred for low-priority batch jobs, (B) autoscaler to prefer filling warm nodes labelled batch=true, (C) storage team to offer remote-backed scratch volumes for batch so PV affinity is less restrictive.
maya: can infra run the descheduler canary at 23:00 UTC tonight? I'll own the runbook and rollback steps.
jon: I'll execute and watch. command: 
jon: kubectl run descheduler-canary -n kube-system --image=registry/descheduler:latest --restart=Never -- 
  --policy-config-file=/etc/descheduler/policy-batch-canary.yaml --v=4
leo: ensure policy excludes pods with annotation "scratch-local=true" and explicitly targets pods older than 24h with low CPU/GPU utilization.
descheduler-bot: policy file tip: set evictionTimeoutSeconds=300 and maxNoOfPodsToEvictPerNode=1 for canary run.
sam: cost team will monitor committed vs actual utilization and update finance if we move capacity between AZs.
maya: timeline: canary tonight, perf microbench tomorrow morning, decide on wider policy change next week if metrics OK.
jon: I'll post the runbook link in #release-war-room and ping infra on call. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks all. tagging cost and storage owners for follow-up. :money_with_wings:
maya: update: billing spike alert just came in. sharing graphs in 10.
jon: ack, thanks everyone.
